decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presented “Add ... bookmarks.” In the round 1 response, the client observed that it “won't even save unless I hand-type a title” and specified “just paste a link.”
decisions.note: At prototype review, requiring a manually entered title prevented URL-only saving; the client supplied the reference-conforming workflow.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presented bookmark adding without automatic page metadata. The round 1 client said the form made them type the title and description and requested that it “pull in the page's name (and ideally a short description/icon) automatically.”
decisions.note: At prototype review, automatic metadata collection was missing and the client requested the related reference requirement.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker explicitly presented “Add and delete bookmarks”; the client confirmed, “I can add one and delete one.”
decisions.note: The presented deletion behavior conforms at prototype review.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker scoped search to “titles, URLs, descriptions, and tags,” omitting bookmark notes. The client only said they could “search them” and requested no search correction.
decisions.note: At prototype review, the enumerated full-text fields omitted the required note field; the client did not express that difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presented an “open-link” action. The client called the remaining experience a good start without disputing link opening.
decisions.note: A dedicated action that navigates to the original URL is functionally equivalent to selecting an item to open it.

decisions.evidence: During the round 1 prototype review, the client reported, “I can see my saved links, search them, favorite them, and sort them.”
decisions.note: The presented prototype visibly supported list sorting, conforming to the sort requirement.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presented adding and deleting but no editing. The client identified that “there's no way to go back and edit a saved link” and requested changing its title, tags, or location after saving.
decisions.note: At prototype review, post-save editing was missing; the client explicitly requested the related editing requirements.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker stated, “Title is no longer required—the domain becomes a fallback if metadata cannot be retrieved.” The client replied that this was “exactly what I was after” and approved it.
decisions.note: The revised implementation allows saving from the URL without requiring a manually entered title.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker enumerated automatic retrieval of “page title, description, and favicon,” but not the required preview image. The client praised the real title and description and approved without mentioning the missing preview image.
decisions.note: At implementation review, the revised metadata behavior remained incomplete relative to the reference; approval did not surface the difference.

decisions.evidence: The round 1 add form exposed title and description before saving; round 2 maker added editing of title and description after saving. The round 2 client confirmed there was now “a proper Edit option.”
decisions.note: Across the revised workflow, auto-collected title and description can be changed before and after saving.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker explicitly scoped editing to “URL, title, description, collection, and tags,” omitting the required note field. The client approved editing of the link, title, tags, and location without identifying the missing note edit.
decisions.note: At implementation review, the editor covered most required fields but not notes; the client did not express or accept that specific difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker stated that editing supports “tags.” The client confirmed the Edit option lets them change “tags” and approved it.
decisions.note: The presented editor supports assigning tags to a bookmark, conforming to the requirement.
